What are you feeling right now?

I could, but I don\'t want to
I waited for the block to end
You\'re tired or it\'s late. Self-control is at its lowest then, and the brain grabs for quick relief.
Stress is pushing you to escape. The urge is a shortcut to feeling better for a few minutes.
Boredom, or avoiding something. The urge fills the gap so you don\'t have to face it.
Loneliness. The urge is standing in for connection.
Anxiety. Your mind wants relief from the worry.
The story you\'re telling yourself is how urges win. Notice it as a story, not a fact.
Urges rise, peak and fade, usually within 10 to 20 minutes. This one will too.
Breathe slowly for one minute: in for 4, out for 6.
Stand up and leave the room you\'re in.
Splash cold water on your face, or take a cold shower.
Walk for ten minutes, ideally outside.
Message or call someone you trust, even about nothing.
Put your phone in another room and leave it there.
Do one small task for ten minutes: a few questions, tidy your desk.
If you can, go to sleep. Tomorrow\'s you will thank you.
Charge your phone outside the bedroom from tonight.
Start your evening block an hour earlier.
Extend a Déchaîner schedule to cover the hour this happened.
Cover your other devices too, or tell someone about them.
Your phone block held, so the urge went offline. Leave the room at the first sign of it, before it builds.
Fix a small start time for your hardest task, so boredom has less room.
Tell one person you trust what you\'re working on.
Move bedtime earlier; short sleep makes every urge stronger.
